subject: Full Plan Autonomous Multi-Provider ACTION Execution

frozen_obligations.evidence: No state-changing provider prerequisite; governed ACTION selects an eligible capability-fit provider.
Governed model execution consumes RouterRequest.v2/RouterDecision.v2; provider/model fields remain Router-owned.
Provider generates proposal only; MUTATION_REQUIRED effects execute through ProductionToolTransport/SingleToolBroker. Legacy paths fail closed.
Router authority preserved; runtime/full_mcp and runtime/mprf product ownership untouched.
No lifecycle/task/fan-in authority moved out of Full Plan.
MPRF remains eligibility/runtime fact source and contains no provider selection invocation.
Full repository regression 1575 PASS, 12 environment/opt-in skips, RC=0.
No task-level provider/model priority; capability-fit test proves either approved provider can win.

findings.evidence: Pre-remediation stage==ACTION provider binding; user-observed WAITING_PROVIDER when Codex unavailable.
findings.impact: Full Plan could not continue autonomously with another eligible provider.
findings.correction: Capability-fit selection with effect/generation capability separation; legacy state-changing mode fails closed into governed Router.
findings.regression: provider router + hybrid flow + full repository regression.

findings.problem: Model generation and state-changing authority were conflated in the Codex-only action path.
findings.impact: Alternative reasoning providers could not participate without being granted inappropriate mutation authority.
findings.correction: Provider-neutral proposal contract; actual writes remain ProductionToolTransport/SingleToolBroker effects with owned scope, authorization, journal, and deterministic verification.
findings.regression: provider action, tool transport, worker executor, Full Plan/Gate suites.

findings.problem: Initial remediation persisted raw provider proposal before complete proposal security scan.
findings.impact: Rejected secret-like generated content could remain in a private artifact.
findings.correction: Complete canonical proposal is security-scanned before private persistence; explicit no-persistence/no-effect regression added.

findings.problem: Initial remediation used explicit NVIDIA/Codex policy rank as a tie breaker.
findings.impact: Would preserve a hidden provider priority despite provider-neutral requirement.
findings.correction: Removed provider-specific rank; narrower capability fit then lexical identity only. Added inverse selection test where Codex wins while NVIDIA is also eligible.

independent_provider_review.reason: Router-selected review provider returned non-JSON analysis despite exact JSON output contract; no verdict from those attempts was used for PASS.

notes: Manual Action remains an emergency/break-glass path but is no longer required for the normal eligible-provider ACTION path.
Current approved provider domain remains NVIDIA and Codex; future providers require approved registry/adapters rather than task hardcoding.
